strategy: point-in-time quality filter on cross-sectional momentum
hypothesis: Excluding low-quality long candidates and high-quality short candidates may reduce momentum crashes and distress exposure without replacing the momentum rank.

existing_evidence.interpretation: Quality was diversifying but unstable and did not survive its prior standalone test.

reason: The source filing cache is not present, and the prior quality signal changed sign sharply between halves. Reusing only its saved headline output cannot support a new conditional portfolio test.

minimum_data_contract.availability: SEC accepted/filed timestamp plus one trading session
minimum_data_contract.flows: true trailing four reported quarters, with duplicate/restatement policy frozen
minimum_data_contract.identifiers: dated CIK-to-symbol mapping including delisted firms
minimum_data_contract.coverage_requirement: at least 80% of otherwise eligible momentum candidates in each evaluation window

pre_registered_test_when_data_exists.candidate: remove the bottom quality quintile from long candidates and top quality quintile from short candidates, then continue down the unchanged momentum rank to fill 20 names per leg
pre_registered_test_when_data_exists.quality_score: equal-weight cross-sectional rank of gross-profit-to-assets and operating-cash-flow-to-assets
pre_registered_test_when_data_exists.rebalance: weekly momentum rebalance using the latest available filing
pre_registered_test_when_data_exists.costs: 15 bps one-way turnover, 3% annual short borrow, whole-share short capacity at $10,000
pre_registered_test_when_data_exists.promotion_rule: Higher net Sharpe and no lower CAGR in both profiles and both early/held-out windows; max drawdown may not worsen; coverage must remain at least 80%.

next_action: Rebuild and version the SEC point-in-time cache before testing or implementing this filter.
